comparator.name: Dentistry
comparator.sourceNotes: Freshly inspected current2026–2027 ACTA OER Arts1.1,9.1,10–11,14 and33mandatory units establish60+60+60=180EC, with no open choice. ACTA delivers the UvA/VU collaborative programme; this case retains the UvA target and generic ordinary full-time pathway. OER1.1 applies to enrolled students from1September2026. Positive BSA requires42first-year EC. First/second-year prescribed order, explicit dental-skills/prevention gates, research-method/preparation gates and preclinical-before-patient-treatment rules are retained. Scientific internship14 is research, not a second clinical placement. ProfessionalConduct1 follows the other179. Current recruitment page advertises2027–2028 but is not substituted for this applicable curriculum.
components: Introduction includes a diagnostic Dutch-language test. A satisfactory test or completion of the required remedial language course is necessary before the module grade is awarded.
Preclinical training develops the practical dental skills needed before patient treatment. At least ninety percent practical attendance is normally required.
Pass first-year Oral Biology and Cariology, Direct Restorations and Dental Skills 1A, and attend all New Patient practicals within Dental Skills 1B.
Pass first-year Oral Biology and Cariology, Direct Restorations and Dental Skills 1A and 1B, and participate in Dental Skills 2A.
Pass first-year Oral Biology and Cariology, Direct Restorations and Dental Skills 1A, and attend all New Patient practicals within Dental Skills 1B.

The compulsory fourteen-credit scientific internship requires Research Methods and Statistics and Preparation for the Scientific Internship. Scientific work includes literature research and/or contribution to research, culminating in a written report.

Pass second-year Prevention, Care Planning, Periodontitis I, Dental Prevention and Dental Skills 2A and 2B. Care of non-complex patients includes oral-health assessment, caries and periodontal treatment, carried out in student pairs with treating and assisting roles.
The patient-care curriculum includes intraoral radiographs. Successful preparatory preclinical practicals are required before patient treatment.

After six months or more without clinical patient care, students must pass both non-patient and patient competency assessments before resuming clinical practicals. Restorative dental work is a clinical and technical learning line, distinct from the scientific research internship.
This compulsory professional-conduct credit is awarded after the other 179 credits. The bachelor prepares for further Dentistry study; it does not itself confer the completed dentist qualification.

exception.reason: UCR offers substantial study of human biology, disease mechanisms, infection, immunity, health psychology and prevention, supported by laboratory and research methods. These are meaningful foundations for oral-health interests. Together these gaps leave dentistry’s defining academic subject matter insufficiently represented.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Screened all151active course identities and read37plausible/original contributions. Three complete24-course trials pass actual term offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four per term, first-yearPPD and advanced-course rules. Biomedical mechanisms, mucosal immunity, general anatomy/imaging, laboratory work, public health, health psychology/consultation, qualitative inquiry, psycholinguistics, ethics, design, robotics and physical/environmental materials receive full supported consideration. Description-only courses were included. No-match follows the combined defining subject shortfall, not missing planning, degree title, professional licence, language, exact equivalence or a matching-course quota.

candidateAssessment.concept: Oral health, disease mechanisms and prevention
candidateAssessment.assessment: The strongest full24-course biomedical trial is mechanically feasible and supplies real cell/organ science, mucosal immunity and host–pathogen research, molecular pathology, pharmacology, wet laboratory practice, epidemiology, pain/health psychology and evidence synthesis. These respond substantially to foundations but do not sustain oral biology, caries/periodontal disease, oral assessment and restorative science as an organising subject. Research flexibility cannot turn general biomedicine into documented taught oral-health inquiry. Academic comparability fails, not scheduling or professional licensing.

candidateAssessment.concept: Patient wellbeing, compassionate communication and accessible oral care
candidateAssessment.assessment: A second whole24-course trial repairs the actual Psycholinguistics offering conflict by using2027h1, and meets all formal rules. Health Psychology covers pain, consultation and treatment decisions; sociology and qualitative interviews address inequality and lived experience; psychopathology, cognition, development, ethics and public persuasion offer complementary substance. Together they implement a general health/patient-experience programme. The oral-care object, oral assessment, dental prevention decisions and treatment planning do not become a sustained academic focus. General compassionate care alone does not establish a programme-level response to dentistry.

candidateAssessment.concept: Precise restorative dental work and technical treatment
candidateAssessment.assessment: A third feasible24-course trial combines biomedical and research foundations with actual physical/chemical materials labs, mineral and biomineralization chemistry, recycling/material analysis, consumer design and robotic manipulation. These provide meaningful material, design and precision methods, considered on their own evidence. Their objects are environmental chemistry, general consumer prototypes and robot kinematics; they do not combine into restorative oral structure/function, dental materials, endodontic or oral-imaging inquiry. This is a substantive subject gap beyond absent supervised treatment or dental qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Dentistry bachelor, taught at ACTA in collaboration with Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, combines biomedical and oral-health science with prevention, restorative dentistry and patient care. The compulsory three-year curriculum includes dental-skills training, supervised treatment, evidence-based dentistry and a scientific internship.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial study of human biology, disease mechanisms, infection, immunity, health psychology and prevention, supported by laboratory and research methods. These are meaningful foundations for oral-health interests. The strongest complete UCR programmes, however, develop general biomedical science, patient experience or materials and technical inquiry without sustained study of oral biology, dental disease and restoration. Together these gaps leave dentistry’s defining academic subject matter insufficiently represented.
